flashcards.q: Geometric reason L1 gives exact zeros and L2 doesn't?
flashcards.a: L1's constraint region (diamond/cross-polytope) has corners exactly on coordinate axes; expanding loss ellipse generically hits a corner first (a coord = 0). L2's region (ball) is smooth everywhere, so it hits a point with all coords nonzero.

flashcards.q: Ridge closed form and why it improves numerical stability?
flashcards.a: w = (X^T X + lambda*I)^-1 X^T y. Adding lambda*I shifts every eigenvalue of X^T X up by lambda, improving the condition number even when X^T X is singular under collinearity.
E[(y - f_hat(x))^2] = Bias(f_hat(x))^2 + Var(f_hat(x)) + sigma^2 (irreducible noise).

High bias: train/val error converge to similarly poor value, small gap -- more data/regularization won't help. High variance: train low, val high, gap doesn't close -- more regularization or more data helps.

flashcards.q: Why does lasso behave unstably under correlated features, and what fixes it?
flashcards.a: It arbitrarily zeros all-but-one of a correlated group near the corner-touching point, unstable across resamples. Elastic net (alpha*L1+(1-alpha)*L2) keeps L2's grouping effect while still allowing exact zeros.

flashcards.q: sklearn's C parameter vs lambda -- what's the relationship and the common mistake?
flashcards.a: C = 1/lambda (inverse strength): small C = MORE regularization. Common mistake: building a hyperparameter grid assuming 'bigger number = more regularization' as with lambda, silently inverting the intended search direction.

flashcards.q: What can regularization never fix, in bias-variance terms?
flashcards.a: Irreducible bias -- it can only trade variance for bias along the tradeoff curve, it cannot beat the achievable error floor set by model class capacity and feature information content.

flashcards.q: Does XGBoost's L1 (reg_alpha) perform feature selection like lasso?
flashcards.a: No -- it penalizes leaf weights within trees whose splits were already chosen by a gain criterion, not feature coefficients; a feature can still appear in many splits. True feature selection needs a separate step (e.g. SHAP-based pruning).

flashcards.q: What is double descent and how confidently should you state it?
flashcards.a: Belkin et al. 2019: test error can decrease again PAST the interpolation threshold as capacity keeps growing, breaking the classical U-shape -- real, empirically documented mainly in high-capacity models, but not a general license to always prefer bigger models.
